clue.text: Poor brute's bleeding, beginning to shave this?

definitions.text: Poor brute's bleeding, beginning to shave this?

indicators.note: something in poor shape is damaged and disordered, so the letters that follow are jumbled

parts.note: taken letter for letter, apostrophe ignored

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of shave

explanation.surface: A man nicks himself badly as he starts his morning shave.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a man with a careful few days' growth is the poor brute who never gets round to shaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Designer stubble is a deliberately cultivated short growth of beard, kept as a fashion look rather than shaved off.

clue.text: Profess to be cleared out

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or not in place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have been completely emptied out.
explanation.definitionFit: To profess a belief is to state it openly, which is to declare it: the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Missile sailor sent up — it was launched in Brazil

parts.note: SAM is a surface-to-air missile

indicators.note: in a down answer, sending something up makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A naval rocket goes up from a launch site in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Launched' suggests a rocket; it means the dance began there.
explanation.definitionFit: The samba is a dance and music style that originated in Brazil, so it was introduced to the world from there.

clue.text: Congratulations, if new clothes look this?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an exclamation praising someone's achievement
second meaning: read literally, the outfit suits its wearer

explanation.surface: A compliment offered to someone trying on a new outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: The same three words work as a cheer and as a literal remark about how clothes look on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal expression of praise, and literally describes clothes that suit the wearer.

clue.text: Not the first to drain jug

indicators.note: not the first tells you the opening letter is missing

parts.note: a sewer is a drain for waste water

explanation.surface: Someone who was not first in line has to empty the jug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drain' looks like a verb about emptying the jug; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An ewer is a large jug with a wide spout, traditionally used with a washbasin.

clue.text: Mammal carrying offspring, depending on the month

indicators.note: something carrying a load holds it inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: a seal is a sea mammal
a son is one offspring

explanation.surface: A pregnant mammal's breeding depends on the time of year.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seasonal varies with the time of year, so whether it happens depends on which month it is.

clue.text: Apart, but not as down

indicators.note: but not tells you to take something away from the word before

parts.note: asunder means into separate pieces
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: A puzzling note comparing what is apart with what is down.
explanation.definitionFit: Under and down both describe a lower position, as in going under or going down.

clue.text: Bore half acceptable to chap that's usually present

indicators.note: half means only part of the word is kept, here its first two letters

parts.note: a bore is a tedious person
OK means acceptable
taken as written
Ken is a man's name, a stock crossword chap

explanation.surface: A dull man is half-tolerated by a colleague who is always around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' suggests attendance, but it means a gift. A book token is a British gift voucher to spend in bookshops.
explanation.definitionFit: A book token is a voucher exchangeable for books, almost always given as a gift.

clue.text: Ruler of the ice and snow?

definitions.text: Ruler of the ice and snow?

parts.words: Ruler of the ice and snow?
parts.note: surface reading: a monarch reigning over a frozen kingdom
setter's reading: a title that also names the largest penguin of the Antarctic ice

explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like a fairy-tale monarch; the title belongs to a bird that lives on Antarctic ice.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is a supreme ruler, and the emperor penguin breeds on Antarctic sea ice, so it reigns in a land of ice and snow.

clue.text: One not entitled to answer, these days

parts.note: a commoner holds no title of nobility
A is the standard abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A person without a title is asked to reply to something about the modern world.
explanation.definitionFit: The Common Era is the neutral name for the current calendar era, the period counted as AD, so it covers the present day.

clue.text: Die, clutching old flag

indicators.note: to clutch something is to hold it tightly within, so one word wraps around another

parts.note: to drop, as in drop dead, is to die suddenly
O is the usual abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone dies still holding an old banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner beside 'old', but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to tire or sag, and to droop is to hang down limply, so both describe energy failing.

clue.text: No sign of volcanic activity about Arthur's Seat

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, as in about-turn, so the phrase is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written
molten rock flowing out is the clearest evidence a volcano is active

explanation.surface: Arthur's Seat, the hill over Edinburgh, shows no hint of an eruption.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur's Seat is a real extinct volcano in Edinburgh, which makes the surface true; but the definition wants King Arthur's own resting place.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend the wounded King Arthur was carried to the isle of Avalon, which became his abode and resting place.

clue.text: Like a general to show boundaries to sailor

indicators.note: to here means placed against, so the second word is joined directly after the first

parts.note: in cricket a ball reaching the boundary after bouncing scores four, so boundaries are fours
tar is old slang for a sailor

explanation.surface: An army officer is told to point out the borders to a navy man.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a hit that reaches the edge of the field along the ground is a boundary worth four runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A full general in the US and British armies wears four stars as a rank insignia, so the rank is called four-star.

clue.text: Very young creature, upsetting me, said "Dash!"

indicators.note: upsetting something tips it over, so in a down-the-page sense the word is turned end to end

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: said points to how a word is spoken rather than how it is written

parts.note: brio is dash or verve; spoken, it gives this spelling

explanation.surface: A baby animal annoys the speaker, who swears mildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dash!' reads as a mild oath, but it is the noun for liveliness.
explanation.definitionFit: An embryo is an animal at its earliest stage of development, before birth or hatching.

clue.text: Shouted at, having drawn off beer under the counter

indicators.note: in a down answer, under places one piece below the other, so it follows it

parts.note: a bar is the counter in a pub
to rack beer is to draw it off its sediment into a fresh cask

explanation.surface: A drinker is shouted at for pouring beer illicitly beneath the counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under the counter' reads as an idiom for secret dealing, but it places one piece below another in the down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To barrack is to jeer or heckle a performer or speaker, so someone barracked has been shouted at.

clue.text: Blow! I was really enjoying myself

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a wild, swinging punch
second meaning: one making hay, a person seizing the good times while they last

explanation.surface: Someone complains that their fun has just been spoiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow!' looks like an exclamation of annoyance; it is the noun for a punch. The second half leans on making hay while the sun shines, that is, enjoying a chance while it lasts.
explanation.definitionFit: A haymaker is a big round-arm punch, and literally someone who makes hay, as people do when they are making the most of good times.

clue.text: See animal swimming for islands

indicators.note: something swimming moves about freely, so the letters change places

parts.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A tourist goes to the islands to watch creatures in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Melanesia is the group of Pacific islands including Fiji, Vanuatu and the Solomons.

clue.text: Report finally filed on one's area of responsibility

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the next word

parts.note: the closing letter of filed
one's read as one is, giving I and IS combined as IS
a patch is the area someone is responsible for, such as a police officer's beat

explanation.surface: A reporter at last files a story about their own territory.
explanation.walkthrough: One's here stands for one is, which shortens to IS. 'Report' looks like the verb; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispatch is an official report or a news story sent in by a correspondent.

clue.text: Wounded one Romeo almost devastated to embrace?

definitions.text: Wounded one Romeo almost devastated to embrace?

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter
an embrace wraps arms around someone, so the rearranged letters wrap around another piece
something devastated is wrecked and scattered, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
Romeo without its last letter
a cut is a wound, so to be cut is to be wounded

explanation.surface: A wounded man whom Romeo, nearly heartbroken, moves to hug.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: in Romeo and Juliet, Romeo's friend is fatally wounded when Romeo steps between the fighters, and Romeo is devastated by his death.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercutio is Romeo's friend in Shakespeare's play, fatally stabbed by Tybalt under Romeo's arm as Romeo tries to part them.

clue.text: Composer set up one crash

indicators.note: in a down answer, set up means raised so it reads from the bottom upward

parts.note: a unit is a single one
to ram is to crash into something

explanation.surface: A musician arranges a single collision on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Bohuslav Martinů was a twentieth-century Czech composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Martinů wrote symphonies, operas and chamber music, which makes him a composer.

clue.text: In first-class condition after amputation, here?

indicators.note: an amputation cuts off an extremity, so the word loses its end

parts.note: clinical can mean spotlessly clean and tidy, as a room in perfect condition is

explanation.surface: A patient is said to be in excellent shape after losing a limb, and asks where they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here?' points back to the surface: the place where an amputation might be carried out.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinic is a medical facility where patients are treated, a plausible setting for the operation the clue describes.

clue.text: Could not evenly take dye

indicators.note: not evenly means the even-numbered letters are dropped, keeping the odd ones

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of could
to bear something is to take or endure it

explanation.surface: A fabric fails to absorb colour uniformly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a dyeing mishap; 'evenly' picks letters instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Cudbear is a purple or violet dye made from lichens, used for wool and silk.

clue.text: Drive idly round Land's End — an afterthought, these?

definitions.text: Drive idly round Land's End — an afterthought, these?

indicators.note: going round something encircles it, so the first word is wrapped around the kept letter

parts.note: to roam is to travel about with no fixed purpose

indicators.note: the end of a word is its closing letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of land
the indefinite article in its shorter form
a postscript, PS, is an afterthought added below a letter

explanation.surface: A motorist wanders around Cornwall's far tip, only remembering the maps at the last minute.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is the westernmost point of mainland England, in Cornwall. The whole clue describes the answer too: what you should consult before such a drive, and too often think of only afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Road maps are charts of routes for motorists, the obvious thing a driver touring around Land's End would need.

clue.text: Small plum in orchard cropped

indicators.note: cropped means trimmed at the edges, so only a run of letters inside the phrase survives

parts.note: the run of letters from the end of plum through the start of orchard

explanation.surface: A little plum grows in a recently harvested orchard.
explanation.definitionFit: Minor means lesser in size or importance, so it is a synonym for small.

clue.text: Some bananas may be spare

definitions.meaning: first meaning: bananas grow and are sold in bunches called hands, so some are in a hand

explanation.surface: Spare bananas are lying about the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: A bunch of bananas is called a hand, which is what makes the first half work.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in hand is available and not yet used, so it is spare; and a cluster of bananas is literally a hand.

clue.text: From US sect, a girl shortly needs husband

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written
a miss is a girl or young woman
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A young woman from an American religious community needs to marry soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' looks like it means soon; it trims a word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amish are a traditionalist Christian group in the US, so Amish describes someone belonging to that sect.

clue.text: Part of face in arch, right?

indicators.note: in places the letter for right inside the word for an arch

parts.note: a bow is a curve or arch
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether a feature of the face is arched correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an arched eyebrow, which is part of the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The brow is the forehead or the ridge over the eyes, a part of the face.

clue.text: Confirm as member of family?

parts.note: a member of a group is in it
kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: Someone is formally accepted into a family.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters for 'in kin' are respaced into a new phrase, which the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: To ink in a pencilled arrangement is to make it definite, so it means to confirm.

clue.text: Short walk to steps and gate

parts.note: to take a turn is to go for a brief stroll
a stile is a set of steps for climbing over a fence or wall

explanation.surface: Directions for a country stroll: walk a little way to the steps and the gate.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnstile is a revolving barrier that admits one person at a time, a kind of gate.

clue.text: Seedy articles found separately in linen

indicators.note: separately in means the pieces are slipped into the word at more than one point

parts.note: body linen is an old term for underclothes
two definite articles, one for each insertion point

explanation.surface: Grubby items turn up here and there among the bed sheets.
explanation.walkthrough: Seedy looks like shabby, but in British English it also means slightly unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling seedy means feeling a bit ill, and under the weather is the idiom for being mildly unwell.
